subject: Integrated species distribution models with presence-only and 'absence-only' datasets

messages.author: 09c288456ab663f2
messages.subject: Integrated species distribution models with presence-only and 'absence-only' datasets
parts:
Hello everyone, 

I'm currently running a series of single-species integrated SDMs for twenty plant species in New Zealand. I have two datasets: presence-only data modeled as a Poisson distribution and presence-absence data modeled as a Binomial distribution. I am using the wrapper functions for INLA and inlabru in the PointedSDMs package to assist with building models from these data. 

This method is working well for the species that have >20 presence records in both data sets. However, several of the species have plenty of presence-only records, but few (<20) or no presence records in the presence-absence data (presumably this is because these are all exotic species that have not become invasive enough in New Zealand to be present in the presence-absence vegetation plots). It seems that the literature on other formulations of presence-absence SDMs agrees that at least 20 records of species presence are required to make robust inference. 

So, I have two questions: 

(1) What is the best option for modeling distributions of species where there is presence-only data, and a data set with a presence-absence observation process that only contains records of species absence? 
(2) Would inference from integrated SDMs constructed from presence-only and presence-absence data be robust if one of these data sets contained fewer than 20 presence records? 

I'm leaning towards modeling these species with INLA as presence-only point process models with random spatial structure modeled as a Matern process with SPDE, but it does seem a shame to throw out information on over 40,000 locations where we know a species is absent. Keen to hear if there are any options for incorporating absence data. 

Many thanks!
Sarah
